reason: The text contains clear instances of the Hebrew people voicing criticism against their leaders. Most prominently, when Moses delays his return from Mount Sinai, the people gather against Aaron (their interim leader) and voice their discontent: 'This Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt—we do not know what happened to him.' They demand that Aaron make them gods to lead them. Additionally, when God appears at Mount Sinai with thunder and lightning, the people request that Moses speak to them rather than God directly, fearing death: 'You speak to us and we will listen, but let not God speak to us, lest we die.' These represent both criticism of leadership (Moses) through expression of doubt and dissatisfaction, and implicit criticism through rejection of direct divine communication.
